sections.cial_corporate_&_developments:
This section tracks direct coverage of Christchurch International Airport, its corporate board and leadership, on-campus commercial property developments, and key regional tourism initiatives.
Include ANY mentions of Christchurch International Airport, Christchurch Airport, or Christchurch International Airport Ltd (CIAL). 
Include ANY mentions of key spokespeople, board members, and senior executives, treating mentions of Sarah Ottrey, Justin Watson, David MacKenzie, Andre Lovatt, Chris Paulsen, Ed Sims, Justin Murray, Gordon Bevan, John O'Dea, Kylie Frisby, Lucy Taylor, Michael Singleton, Nick Flack, Rhys Boswell, Tim May, and Yvonne Densem as direct mentions the corporate.
Include coverage of former Board Chair Catherine Drayton or former Chief Executive Malcolm Johns ONLY when discussed in direct relation to their historical roles, past decisions, or corporate legacy at CIAL.
Include coverage regarding on-campus retail, industrial, environmental, or land developments, specifically Spitfire Square, Dakota Park, and Mustang Park.
Include coverage of Isaac Conservation Park ONLY when discussed in direct relation to Christchurch Airport development or environmental offsets.
Include stories about Kōwhai Park solar farm project, or other large-scale solar farms in New Zealand.
Include coverage of regional tourism campaigns and frameworks led by or involving CIAL, specifically Kia Ora South or South, as well as general Christchurch visitor numbers or commentary from Canterbury Tourism figures.
Include coverage of the New Zealand Airports Association (NZAA) in any operational or industry context.
SECTION-SPECIFIC EXCLUSIONS
Exclude articles that merely use the airport as a physical geographical landmark or direction (e.g., "accident occurred near Christchurch Airport").
Exclude news focusing on former CIAL employees unless their past statements or current activities directly impact active corporate operations.
Exclude general operations, reviews, or promotional marketing of the Sudima Hotel or the Airport Hotel unless directly tied to CIAL joint ventures, land acquisitions, or terminal developments.
Exclude standard daily weather updates, regional temperature summaries, wind alerts, or heatwave reports that mention the airport simply because it is the site of the meteorological recording station.
Exclude any routine business, construction, or real estate listings concerning Stonewood Homes.
Exclude standard operational listings such as routine airline timetable listings, generic retail promotions, job vacancies, or recruitment notices that have no journalistic news value.
GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
Letters (unless from someone prominent such as a politician or company executive)
Talkback callers
Media Releases / Advertorials and advertising features
Q&A or advice articles
Videos on online media outlets where there is only a short snippet.
Exclude online Syndication where specified by the brief parameters (specifically syndicated online repeats and global view duplicates for general CIAL news).
sections.aviation_industry:
This section tracks broader aviation sector trends, sustainability frameworks, competitor airport activities, technological innovations, and relevant community or social media conversations.

Include coverage of "Air New Zealand" or "Air NZ" ONLY if the airline is discussed in direct relation to at least one of the following topics evaluated individually: rising airfares, cost pressures, flight cancellations, schedule changes, jet fuel crisis, increasing capacity, cutting flights, or flight disruptions
Include stories or articles that contain the exact phrase 'sustainable aviation' or the exact phrase 'smart airport'.
Include coverage of global and national environmental, decarbonization, or sustainability frameworks in the aviation sector, specifically the Airport Carbon Accreditation (ACA) programme, the Jet Zero Council, and Sustainable Aviation Aotearoa.
Include stories about the fuel crisis that impacts the aviation industry in New Zealand. 
Include coverage of "Air New Zealand" or "Air NZ" ONLY if the airline is discussed in direct relation to at least one of the following topics evaluated individually: climate change, climate action, climate crisis.
Include coverage of Qantas ONLY when discussed in direct relation to climate change, climate action, or climate crisis.
Include coverage regarding airfares or air fares ONLY IF the article has a clear New Zealand focus and is in direct relation to price increases, spikes, or sudden pricing surges.
Include coverage of airport environmental initiatives globally or nationally addressing biodiversity, biofuels, circular economy, green energy, clean energy, and renewable energy.
Include coverage of aviation decarbonization pathways, including carbon management, carbon accreditation, carbon offsets, carbon removals, climate change, climate adaptation, decarbonisation, emissions reduction, emissions trading, green hydrogen, net zero targets, and science-based targets.
Include coverage of the Just Transition programme ONLY when referenced in relation to New Zealand, Australia, or the Pacific.
Include coverage of environmental issues such as air pollution, aircraft emissions, noise contours, oil spills, and water supply pollution ONLY when discussed in direct relation to airlines and airports. Coverage of noise contours MUST have a clear Christchurch focus in relation to property/residential development.
Include coverage of commercial and pricing regulatory negotiations between airports and airlines within New Zealand.
Include stories regarding development or construction when Auckland Airport, Wellington Airport, Queenstown Airport, Dunedin Airport, Invercargill Airport, and regional hubs (Hamilton, Hawke's Bay, Palmerston North, New Plymouth, Rotorua, Kaikoura, Tauranga, Nelson, Timaru, Alexandra) are mentioned. 
Include coverage of Lonely Planet or general visitor numbers impacting Canterbury or South Island regional entry points.
Include coverage of advanced aviation technologies, specifically AI, digital transformation, digital technologies, self-service airports, smart aprons, or Intelligent AiPRON.
Include coverage of CIAL-backed public events, sports programs, and regional sponsorships, specifically Special Olympics New Zealand, the 2025 National Summer Games (NSG Ōtautahi Christchurch), and mentions of Liz Fitzgerald.

SECTION-SPECIFIC EXCLUSIONS
Exclude general service, route, merger, or joint-venture announcements for competitor airlines (e.g., Cathay Pacific, China Airlines, China Southern, Emirates, Fiji Airways, Jetstar, Origin Pacific, Pacific Blue, Singapore Airlines) if they mention biofuel, unless discussing broader airport environmental programs.
Exclude general consumer travel marketing, passenger reviews, or flight route announcements for peer airports or airlines unless they explicitly discuss pricing negotiations, climate strategy, or major runway/terminal infrastructure construction.
Exclude the term "biofuel" when discussed in standard, non-aviation industrial or agricultural contexts.
Exclude coverage of broad international climate conferences (such as COP) unless New Zealand aviation policy is a central theme.
Exclude general, non-corporate social media posts using the word "Christchurch" or "Airport" that do not mention CIAL corporate business, regional airport development, or the listed tracked campaign accounts/handles.
Exclude standard promotional, non-news posts from unrelated peer airports on social media platforms.
GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
Letters (unless from someone prominent such as a politician or company executive)
Talkback callers
Media Releases / Advertorials and advertising features
Q&A or advice articles
Videos on online media outlets where there is only a short snippet.
Exclude online Syndication where specified by the brief parameters (specifically syndicated online repeats and global view duplicates for general CIAL news).
sections.safety_&_emergency_management:
This section tracks emergency infrastructure, airline operational emergencies, legislative civil defense frameworks, and wildlife hazard mitigation.
Include coverage of technical safety systems and training drills, including disabled aircraft recovery (DAR), Engineered Materials Arresting System (EMAS) or EMASMAX cellular cement blocks, Runway End Safety Area (RESA) compliance, development, or runway overshoot/runway overrun incidents.
Include coverage of emergency landing protocols, emergency drills/exercises, terminal evacuations, terminal fire alarms, gas leaks, risk management, and safety process improvements.
Include coverage of Transport Accident Investigation Commission (TAIC) investigations, safety reports, safety recommendations, or infrastructure investments linked directly to safety or emergency response.
Include coverage regarding adverse weather impacting airline operations, groundings, or airport closures ONLY IF the article has a clear New Zealand focus.
Include coverage of critical safety issues occurring on aircraft or flights, including aircraft emergencies, emergency landings, safety concerns, security incidents, engine faults, engine problems, engine fires, engine failures, onboard fires, landing gear faults, technical problems, or emergency exit openings.
Include coverage regarding minimum standard emergency management ONLY IF the article has a clear New Zealand focus.
Include coverage regarding overhaul of emergency management systems ONLY IF the article has a clear New Zealand focus.
Include coverage regarding wildlife hazards, incidents, statistical reports, and runway management strategies concerning bird strikes in New Zealand or globally.
SECTION-SPECIFIC EXCLUSIONS
Exclude minor flight delays due to standard seasonal weather such as fog, rain, or passenger boarding delays.
Exclude routine airport maintenance announcements (e.g., repainting runway lines, standard terminal cleaning, standard terminal upgrades) that do not result in airport closure, flight diversions, or emergency responses.
GENERAL EXCLUSIONS
Letters (unless from someone prominent such as a politician or company executive)
Talkback callers
Media Releases / Advertorials and advertising features
Q&A or advice articles
Videos on online media outlets where there is only a short snippet.
Exclude online Syndication where specified by the brief parameters (specifically syndicated online repeats and global view duplicates for general CIAL news).
